[[File:Stratmann Martin 8930.jpg|thumb|Stratmann in 2018]]
'''Martin Stratmann''' (born 20 April 1954 in [[Essen, Germany|Essen, West Germany]]) is a German electrochemist and [[materials science|materials scientist]]. He is one of the directors at the [[Max Planck Institute for Iron Research|Max-Planck-Institut für Eisenforschung]] (Max-Planck-Institute for Iron Research) in Düsseldorf since 2000, and heads its department of Interface Chemistry and Surface Engineering.<ref name="e319">{{cite web | title=Interface Chemistry and Surface Engineering | website=Startseite | date=11 March 2024 | url=https://www.mpie.de/InterfaceChemistry | access-date=9 June 2025}}</ref>

Stratmann was the vice president of the [[Max Planck Society]] from 2008 and its president from July 2014<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpg.de/468104/eisenforschung_wissM2-|title=Stratmann, Martin|website=www.mpg.de}}</ref> until 22 June 2023. 

== Professional career==
After finishing his ''[[Abitur]]'' (A-levels) in 1973 at the grammar school in [[Traben-Trarbach]] (Rhineland-Palatinate, south-west Germany), and after his military service, Stratmann studied chemistry at the [[Ruhr University Bochum]].<ref name="r679">{{cite web | title=Materials Research Department | website=Materials Research Department | date=18 July 2023 | url=https://mrd.rub.de/alumni/ | language=de | access-date=9 June 2025}}</ref> Stratmann received his diploma about [[Nuclear magnetic resonance|NMR]]-analysis of the diffusion of anions and cations in [[Strontium chloride|SrCl<sub>2</sub>]] in 1979. He did his doctorate on the topic of electrochemical analysis of phase transitions in corrosion layers at the Max-Planck-Institut für Eisenforschung (MPIE) in 1982. Between 1983 and 1984, he continued his research at the Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland (USA) as a scholarship holder of the Max Planck Society. After his return to the MPIE, he worked until 1987 as a scientific assistant in the group of corrosion science. In 1987, he became head of this group. In 1994 Stratmann was appointed to a professorship for corrosion and surface engineering as a successor of H. Kaesche at the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg|Friedrich Alexander University in Erlangen-Nürnberg]] (Bavaria) and remained there till 1999. In 2000, Stratmann returned to the MPIE as a scientific member and director of the department "Interface Chemistry and Surface Engineering".<ref>[http://www.electrochem.org/meetings/biannual/216/ecs_lecture/ Corrosion Protection of Steel]</ref> Two years later he was chosen to be the chief-executive (rotationally until 2010).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mpie.de/index.php?id=802|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120207015911/http://www.mpie.de/index.php?id=802|url-status=dead|title=Department "Interface Chemistry and Surface Engineering" at the Max-Planck-Institut für Eisenforschung|archivedate=7 February 2012}}</ref>

From 2006 until 2008, Stratmann chaired the chemical-physical-technical section of the Max Planck Society and was appointed vice president of the Max Planck Society in 2008. He is the manager of the [[Minerva Foundation]], an affiliate of the Max Planck Society, since 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mpg.de/martin-stratmann |title=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft President Biography |date=15 April 2019 |quote=Since 2008, he has also been the Scientific Director of the Minerva Foundation, which was established as a subsidiary of the Max Planck Society in the 1960s and is the flagship of German-Israeli scientific cooperation.}}</ref>

== Research interests==
The research interests of Martin Stratmann concentrate on electrochemistry and corrosion science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://edoc.mpg.de/624988|title=Electrochemistry: Rebirth of a science|website=edoc.mpg.de}}</ref> He connects electrochemical, spectroscopic and interface analytical methods and was the first one who used the [[scanning Kelvin probe]] technique in corrosion science.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Salgin|first1=Bekir|last2=Vogel|first2=Dirk|last3=Pontoni|first3=Diego|last4=Schröder|first4=Heiko|last5=Schönberger|first5=Bernd|last6=Stratmann|first6=Martin|last7=Reichert|first7=Harald|last8=Rohwerder|first8=Michael|date=1 January 2012|title=A scanning Kelvin probe for synchrotron investigations: the in situ detection of radiation-induced potential changes|journal=Journal of Synchrotron Radiation|volume=19|issue=1|pages=48–53|doi=10.1107/S0909049511047066|pmid=22186643|issn=0909-0495|doi-access=free|bibcode=2012JSynR..19...48S }}</ref> With this method he was able to show that electrochemical reaction analysis is possible even under ultrathin electrolytic films and non-conducting coatings. With the help of the Kelvin probe, Stratmann was able to explain the atmospheric corrosion of iron and iron based alloys, and the de-adhesion of polymer coatings of reactive metallic surfaces. With the insight that the formation of electrochemical elements and especially the reduction of molecular oxygen is the key factor to understand the stability of metal-polymer bonds, Stratmann and his team developed new interface-chemical concepts to increase the stability of these bonds which finally lead to self-healing processes of defect interfaces.<ref>{{cite journal| doi=10.1016/S0300-9440(98)00010-1 | volume=34 | issue=1–4 | title=Self-assembling adhesion promoters for corrosion resistant metal polymer interfaces | year=1998 | journal=Progress in Organic Coatings | pages=1–12 | last1 = Maege | first1 = Iris | last2 = Jaehne | first2 = Evelin | last3 = Henke | first3 = Axel | last4 = Hans-Juergen | first4 = P Adler | last5 = Bram | first5 = Christian | last6 = Jung | first6 = Christian | last7 = Stratmann | first7 = Martin}}</ref> These concepts were also transferred into industrial applications.

== Recognition ==
<!--* 1969 Award of the Ruhr University Bochum for the best diploma thesis of this year-->
* 1985 [[Otto Hahn Medal]] of the Max Planck Society for the research on the reactions of phase interfaces and solid state bodies during the growth of corrosion layers<ref name="e823" />
* 1990 Masing Award of the German Society for Material Science (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Materialkunde) for the research on corrosion reactions under thin electrolyte films<ref name="o885">{{cite web | title=The President – And His Start in Office | url=https://www.mpg.de/8415018/S005_Max-Planck-Community_076-078.pdf | access-date=9 June 2025}}</ref>
* 1995 DECHEMA Award of the Max Buchner Research Foundation<ref name="t520">{{cite web | title=Mitglieder | website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina | date=29 June 2023 | url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/martin-stratmann/ | language=de | access-date=9 June 2025}}</ref>
* 2005 [[Willis R. Whitney|Willis Rodney Whitney]] Award of the National Association of Corrosion Engineers (NRACE)<ref name="t520" />
* 2005 UR Evans Award of the British Institute of Corrosion<ref name="e823">{{cite web | title=Stratmann, Martin | website=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft zur Förderung der Wissenschaften | date=6 June 2025 | url=https://www.mpg.de/468104/eisenforschung_wissM2 | access-date=9 June 2025}}</ref>
* 2008 H. H. Uhlig Award of the Electrochemical Society<ref name="e823" />

Stratmann is a fellow of the Electrochemical Society<ref name="i083">{{cite web | title=Stratmann, Martin | website=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft zur Förderung der Wissenschaften | date=6 June 2025 | url=https://www.mpg.de/468104/sustainable-materials-stratmann | access-date=9 June 2025}}</ref> and member of Acatech (German Academy of Engineering Sciences)<ref name="u779">{{cite web | title=Martin Stratmann | website=acatech | date=2 June 2025 | url=https://www.acatech.de/person/martin-stratmann-56410/ | language=de | access-date=9 June 2025}}</ref> and the [[North Rhine-Westphalian Academy of Sciences, Humanities and the Arts]]. Together with Allan Bard, he is editor in chief of the comprehensive encyclopedia of electrochemistry.
